headline_marked: Jamaat slams [[State Minister Ishraque Hossain for brandishing pistol]] during drug drive
headline: Jamaat slams State Minister Ishraque Hossain for brandishing pistol during drug drive
summary: The party called the act 'unlawful' and a signal of a 'reign of terror', while the DMP is now probing the incident.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs and Dhaka-6 MP Ishraque Hossain has come under fire for brandishing a pistol during an anti-drug drive in Dhaka's Gendaria area.
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has strongly criticised the act, stating that uploading a video of the incident on Facebook showed an intention to instill fear among the public.
Jamaat Assistant Secretary General Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair argued that under existing arms laws, licensed firearms cannot be used to create public fear, except for personal security.
The party further alleged that the minister's actions violated his oath of office and could encourage criminal elements, describing the conduct of his bodyguards as aggressive.
In response to the controversy, the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has confirmed that the display of arms during the drive is being investigated.
Meanwhile, State Minister Ishraque Hossain has defended his actions, suggesting in some reports that he would use bamboo sticks instead of firearms for future drives to destroy drug dens.
caption:
A State Minister brandishing a pistol during a drug drive? Jamaat calls it a 'reign of terror'.

State Minister for Liberation War Affairs and Dhaka-6 MP Ishraque Hossain has come under fire for brandishing a pistol during an anti-drug drive in Dhaka's Gendaria area.

Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has strongly criticised the act, stating that uploading a video of the incident on Facebook showed an intention to instill fear among the public.

Jamaat Assistant Secretary General Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair argued that under existing arms laws, licensed firearms cannot be used to create public fear, except for personal security.

The party further alleged that the minister's actions violated his oath of office and could encourage criminal elements, describing the conduct of his bodyguards as aggressive.

In response to the controversy, the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has confirmed that the display of arms during the drive is being investigated.

Meanwhile, State Minister Ishraque Hossain has defended his actions, suggesting in some reports that he would use bamboo sticks instead of firearms for future drives to destroy drug dens.

headline_marked: Indian air ambulance [[door opens mid-air]], patient dies after landing in Dhaka
headline: Indian air ambulance door opens mid-air, patient dies after landing in Dhaka
summary: A mechanical fault caused the aircraft's door to partially open at 12,000ft, leading to an emergency landing at Shahjalal International Airport.
details: An Indian air ambulance made an emergency landing in Dhaka after a mechanical fault caused its door to open mid-flight over Bangladesh.
The aircraft was traveling from Agartala, Tripura, to Kolkata, West Bengal, when a fault in the cabin pressurisation system caused the main door to be damaged and partially open.
The incident occurred while the plane was flying at an altitude of 12,000ft, prompting the pilot to declare an emergency and seek permission to land at Shahjalal International Airport.
Airport authorities placed firefighting and rescue vehicles, ambulances, and doctors on standby to handle the potential emergency upon landing.
The aircraft landed safely at 1:40pm Dhaka time, and all crew members and other occupants on board were safe.
The patient on board was promptly transferred to Kurmitola Multicare Specialised Hospital, where doctors later declared them dead.
The aircraft, a 1994 Beechcraft King Air, was previously owned by the Haryana state government and is now operated by SKB Intracon.
